displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that resurrection belief can be reasonable, without being compulsory, if a carefully delimited cumulative historical case raises divine resurrection above serious competing explanations.

novelty.explanation: This narrows the live conclusion and repairs the gap between possible disagreement and independently adequate warrant.

premises.text: Reasonable belief requires neither certainty nor universal persuasion, but it does require evidence that independently clears a publicly defensible threshold.

novelty.explanation: This preserves the lower threshold while adding the negative side's objective adequacy requirement.

premises.text: Early and sincere resurrection proclamation has evidential value only to the extent that provenance, independence, and experiential content can be historically supported.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the affirmative's broad testimonial claim by incorporating the strongest source-access objections.

premises.text: Costly commitment primarily supports sincerity; its additional value depends upon establishing that witnesses possessed firsthand access and remained independent.

novelty.explanation: This accepts the sincerity distinction and specifies when costly commitment could gain further evidential importance.

premises.text: Ordinary alternatives may be combined, but their adequacy must be tested against only those historical facts established independently of the resurrection narratives' theological conclusions.

novelty.explanation: This corrects the tendency to treat every reported detail as a secure, jointly independent explanandum.

premises.text: A metaphysical case for divine agency can adjust explanatory availability only if it establishes relevant agency and interaction, not merely an abstract first cause.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the compressed transition from pure actuality to a resurrection-capable personal agent.

conclusion.text: Accordingly, accepting resurrection may be reasonable for an evaluator who finds the restricted historical facts, source analysis, and independent divine-agency case cumulatively stronger than the remaining alternatives.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion proportionately extends the affirmative case without claiming certainty or mandatory agreement.

newArguments.title: Discriminating Evidence Matrix
newArguments.text: Instead of asking whether one ordinary theory explains every narrative detail, construct a matrix containing only independently supported facts and score each hypothesis for explanatory scope, auxiliary assumptions, source dependence, and expected counterevidence. Resurrection need not dominate every cell to remain reasonable, but it must outperform mixed ordinary accounts on enough well-supported facts to compensate for its lower prior probability. This method makes the comparison transparent and prevents disputed narrative details from silently determining the result.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a formal comparative method not articulated in the locked participant moves.

newArguments.title: Asymmetric Defeater Commitment
newArguments.text: A responsible affirmative case should announce beforehand what discoveries would materially reduce confidence: strong evidence of literary dependence behind alleged independent appearances, authenticated early recantation, identifiable remains, or evidence that key traditions developed substantially later. Publicly accepting such defeaters gives the historical claim meaningful vulnerability while avoiding the implausible demand that a single ambiguous artifact instantly settle every connected proposition. The resulting position is testable through proportional revision even when definitive experimental repetition is unavailable.

novelty.explanation: This develops the live falsifiability reply into explicit, proportionate confidence-revision commitments.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that withholding resurrection belief is reasonable because the available evidence does not overcome source uncertainty, ordinary error mechanisms, and the unusually demanding explanatory leap to divine action.

novelty.explanation: This integrates the negative burden, source limitations, and comparative case into one proportionate thesis.

premises.text: The negative need not establish nonoccurrence; it must show that affirmative acceptance lacks enough warrant after relevant alternatives and uncertainties are included.

novelty.explanation: This directly extends the accurately framed motion-level burden.

premises.text: Historical testimony can justify beliefs, but evidential weight decreases when authorship, independence, witness access, transmission, and reconciliation remain uncertain.

novelty.explanation: This repairs any categorical dismissal of ancient testimony by presenting a graduated reliability analysis.

premises.text: Sincerity and sacrifice support commitment, yet accuracy additionally requires reliable access, causal interpretation, and protection against shared social or transmission error.

novelty.explanation: This develops the negative side's strongest distinction into an explicit multi-stage evidential requirement.

premises.text: Mixed ordinary mechanisms remain available because different report features may arise through different combinations of experience, interpretation, memory, authorship, and transmission.

novelty.explanation: This strengthens the ordinary-alternatives case without requiring one mechanism to explain every reported feature.

premises.text: Invoking divine action requires evidence for relevant agency and interaction beyond identifying an unexplained event or proposing an abstract metaphysical cause.

novelty.explanation: This replaces an overly restrictive scientific-demonstration demand with a broader independent-warrant requirement.

conclusion.text: Therefore, withholding acceptance is proportionate unless source reliability, comparative explanatory advantage, and relevant divine agency are established strongly enough to overcome the accumulated uncertainty.

novelty.explanation: This conclusion combines the negative burdens without claiming that resurrection was disproved.

newArguments.title: Correlated Testimony Discount
newArguments.text: Multiple reports should increase confidence according to their independence, not merely their number. If later accounts share traditions, communities, theological expectations, or literary sources, apparent multiplication may represent correlated transmission rather than separate confirmation. A structured dependence discount would assign less cumulative weight when reports plausibly inherit the same interpretive framework. This does not render the testimony worthless; it prevents numerical accumulation from overstating how much genuinely independent evidence supports the resurrection inference.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a dependence-sensitive aggregation rule not explicitly developed in the participant exchange.

newArguments.title: Prediction Without Courtroom Analogy
newArguments.text: The negative can avoid importing courtroom standards by comparing expected evidence under rival hypotheses. If a relational deity intended a resurrection to ground broadly accessible belief, clearer provenance, independent contemporary attestation, durable corroboration, or repeated accessible disclosure would be more expected than the record described here. Ordinary tradition development predicts ambiguity and dependence more readily. This remains a probabilistic argument: competing divine purposes could weaken the prediction, but they require independent specification rather than serving as unrestricted explanations for any evidential pattern.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the courtroom comparison and specifies the relational evidence argument as a defeasible prediction.
